items.text: Broncos ruled out RB RJ Harvey for Sunday vs. Chiefs; WR Jaylen Waddle listed as questionable.
items.opportunity: Increased carries/snaps for Dobbins and Coleman.

items.text: Eagles ruled out WR DeVonta Smith but RB Saquon Barkley has no injury designation for SNF vs. Washington.
items.why: Friday injury report clear for Barkley; Smith out.
items.implication: Barkley full workload; more targets to Goedert/others without Smith.
items.opportunity: Barkley snaps/carries/red-zone; Goedert route share up.

items.text: Lamar Jackson officially has no injury designation and will start Sunday at Buffalo after missing three games with high ankle sprain; full participant.
items.implication: Unlocks Ravens offense; major QB upgrade and WR boost.
items.opportunity: Higher pass volume, designed runs, red-zone for Flowers/Henry/Andrews.

items.text: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice has no injury designation and is expected to play Sunday vs. Broncos after hamstring absence.
items.implication: Reclaims WR1 targets in KC offense.
items.opportunity: High target share, red-zone usage with Mahomes.

items.text: Buccaneers ruled out WR Emeka Egbuka for Sunday’s game vs. the Falcons.
items.why: Concussion/foot; cleared concussion but foot keeps him out.
items.implication: Bucs WR depth thins; Godwin/Irving target bumps possible.
items.opportunity: Increased routes/targets for remaining TB pass-catchers.

items.text: We've taken Emeka Egbuka (concussion, foot), Carnell Tate (shoulder), Tyjae Spears (knee), AJ Brown (knee) out as of now; see fallout in ETR projections.
items.why: Injury designations and history (AJ knee red flag).
items.implication: Projection adjustments; beneficiaries in those offenses.
items.opportunity: Role expansion for backups/handcuffs and remaining skill players.

items.text: Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) and WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) are off the injury report and good to go vs. Vikings.
Brian Thomas Jr went 87-1282-10 as a rookie in 2024. Fast forward 20 games, and he's in the Konata Mumpfield/Troy Franklin tier of Wk 8 projections.
items.implication: Fade or sit in Week 8; opportunity/efficiency issues.

items.text: Josh Jacobs going the Ashton Jeanty route of strong fantasy value. High-value touches are king; in two games since suspension, three carries inside the 5 and 13 targets.
items.why: Goal-line and target volume driving value despite efficiency.
items.implication: Sustainable RB1/2 floor via opportunity, not YPC.
items.opportunity: Inside-5 carries + receiving work; Jeanty similar inefficient but high-value profile.

items.text: Jaylen Waddle is on my HATE list this week. The production hasn’t been there, and the Chiefs have allowed just ONE touchdown to an opposing WR all season (JSN).
items.why: Poor recent production + elite Chiefs WR defense; also Q.

items.text: Zay Flowers is my WR5 this week. Lamar Jackson is expected back, and I LOVE what that means for Flowers.
items.why: Lamar unlock in potential track-meet vs Bills.
items.implication: Start with confidence as high-end WR1/2.

items.text: RB Loves: Derrick Henry (RB6 @BUF), Chase Brown (RB8 vs TEN), Josh Jacobs (RB11 vs CAR), Breece Hall. Hates: Saquon Barkley (RB20 @WSH), Omarion Hampton (RB34 @LAR), Tony Pollard.
items.why: Favorable run matchups and roles for loves; usage/role/matchup concerns for hates.
items.opportunity: Henry goal-line/history; Brown TD regression; Jacobs volume.

items.text: In the 2 games since Caleb Williams returned, Colston Loveland is averaging a 30% target share and 19.2 PPG; leads TE utilization, top-5 finishes both weeks.
items.why: Elite target share and production with Williams.

items.text: I am FULL CHUB on Mr. Hubbard! Chuba Hubbard has been this year’s Javonte Williams.
items.why: Strong usage/efficiency profile akin to prior Javonte breakout.
